E1.text:
Therefore replacing $H_1$ by $H_1'$ gives a nontoroidal graph. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments $A$ and added edges $E$, gives the $26{,}633$ possible forms of $H_1$. Adjoining $H_2$ to each gives all possible $G$, and \supp{E1} excludes them all. Hence no bridge contains such a path.
\end{proof}

E2.text:
The graph $G$ has $K$ as a minor by retaining $B$, the edge $cd$,
and shortening $apc,brd$ to $ac,bd$. Thus $K$ has no $K_5$ minor.
By the equivalence just proved, replacing $B$ by an allowed minor $B'$
gives a nontoroidal graph whenever $B'+ac+cd+bd$ is nonplanar.
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments $a,b,c,d$ and
added edges $ac,cd,bd$, therefore lists all $15{,}626$ candidate forms
of $B$. Adjoining $\Psi_1$ and $af$ to each candidate gives a graph
with a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E2}, a
contradiction. Therefore $B$ does have a disk drawing in the order $a,b,d,c$, and Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation} implies $D$ is a single vertex.
\end{proof}

E3.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. The
possible bridges are then those with one interior vertex and
the forms in Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}.
At most three four-attachment bridges have the same attachment
set, since four would give $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor.
We combine these bridges with disjoint interiors, subject to
the attachment restrictions and Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}.
A bridge containing $P_m$ includes that path and all
$\Psi_1$-bridges meeting its interior, so its form also
accounts for the length of $P_m$. These enumerations are
recorded in~\supp{E3,~E4}. The next lemma says that if a bridge with three attachments,
together with four vertices having those attachments as their
neighborhood, is toroidal, then adding some two edges between
its attachments gives a planar graph.

These give $72$ labeled forms. Among the eighteen triples meeting
both $A_1,A_2$, twelve contain an edge $P_i$, from three choices of
that edge and four choices of the third vertex. The other six
contain none, giving $12\cdot3+6\cdot6=72$. Form graphs by adding
these bridges to $\Psi_1$ with disjoint interiors, using at most
three on any one triple by Lemma~\ref{dis:counts} and at most five
in total. By Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation}, there is at most
one four-attachment vertex on each set $\{s_i,t_i,s_j,t_j\}$.
We also allow any subset of the six edges $s_it_j$ with $i\ne j$.
We retain only graphs satisfying
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a) and
Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation}, and exclude disjoint
$s_i$--$t_j$ and $s_j$--$t_i$ paths through distinct bridges by
Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order}. The obstruction check in~\supp{E3}
leaves only $\mathfrak T_{48}$ and $\mathfrak T_{58}$. Neither graph
has a four-attachment bridge. Together with $\mathfrak T_5$,
$\mathfrak T_{68}$ and $\mathfrak T_{69}$, these give the graphs in
the statement.
\end{proof}

E4.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. The
possible bridges are then those with one interior vertex and
the forms in Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}.
At most three four-attachment bridges have the same attachment
set, since four would give $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor.
We combine these bridges with disjoint interiors, subject to
the attachment restrictions and Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}.
A bridge containing $P_m$ includes that path and all
$\Psi_1$-bridges meeting its interior, so its form also
accounts for the length of $P_m$. These enumerations are
recorded in~\supp{E3,~E4}. The next lemma says that if a bridge with three attachments,
together with four vertices having those attachments as their
neighborhood, is toroidal, then adding some two edges between
its attachments gives a planar graph.

Exclude a graph if a degree-three interior vertex has adjacent neighbors, or if both $s_it_j$ and $s_jt_i$ occur for $i\ne j$, by Lemmas~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a) and~\ref{dis:opposite-order}. If $s_mt_m$ is absent, require a bridge with both $s_m,t_m$ among its attachments, since $P_m$ lies in such a bridge. We do not choose the paths inside the candidates or require three disjoint $s_m$--$t_m$ paths. The family therefore includes additional graphs, but every graph under consideration occurs in it. Since some $P_m$ is not an edge, \eqref{dis:shortest} gives $s_mt_m\notin E(G)$. We therefore consider candidates with at least one of these three edges absent. Among those whose bridges all have at most one interior vertex, the enumeration~\supp{E4} leaves $\mathfrak T_{32},\quad \mathfrak T_{43},\quad
\mathfrak T_{61}$. Among those with a bridge of form $T,S$ or $Q$, it leaves $\mathfrak T_{38},\quad \mathfrak T_{45},\quad
\mathfrak T_{48},\quad \mathfrak T_{66},\quad
\mathfrak T_{67}$.

No candidate with a four-cycle form remains. These checks cover all the bridge forms, with graphs containing both a $T,S,Q$ form and a four-cycle form included in both checks. Every other candidate has a torus embedding, a $K_5$ minor, a cut of order at most two or a proper nontoroidal minor, as recorded in~\supp{E4}. The same family with all three edges $s_mt_m$ present gives
$\mathfrak T_{48}$ and $\mathfrak T_{58}$, already covered by
Theorem~\ref{dis:endpoint-only}. The three checks above
therefore give the stated list.
\end{proof}

E5.text:
Finally, apply Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}
with the six choices of $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$, the added edges
$ac,bd$, and the required subdivision edges and planar
completions established above. This lists every possible $B$.
Restoring the twin subgraphs $J_1\cup J_2$, the edges $cf,ed$,
and the chosen exterior configuration gives the $1{,}586$ candidates for
$G$. The checks in~\supp{E5} leave only
$G\cong\mathfrak T_{21}$ or $G\cong\mathfrak T_{63}$.
\end{proof}

E6.text:
The paths $P_x,P_y,s_xps_y,t_xrt_y$ give $B\cup C$ as a
minor of $G$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. It is nonplanar by
Lemma~\ref{dis:four-cycles}, and every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision
in it uses $s_yt_y$, since
deleting this edge leaves the planar graph
$B\cup s_ys_xt_xt_y$.
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with $H_0=C$, therefore lists
the $1{,}378$ possible forms of $B$, with $s_yt_y$ required in the subdivision.
Up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$, the enumeration in~\supp{E6}
leaves only one form for which $B\cup K_4[A]$ is
three-connected, there are no disjoint $s_x$--$t_y$ and
$s_y$--$t_x$ paths, and no degree-three interior vertex has
adjacent neighbors in $G$. Its interior is $\{p',q',v\}$,
where
\[
N(p')=N(q')=\{s_x,s_y,v\},
\]
and its remaining edges are $vt_x,vt_y$.

E7.text:
It remains to determine $B$. Shortening the paths $apc,brd$
to $ac,bd$ and retaining $P_x=cd$ gives $K$ as a minor of
$G$, so $K$ has no $K_5$ minor. It is nonplanar, and every
$K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it
uses $cd$, since $K-cd=B+ac+bd$ is planar. Let $H_0$ be the
path $a-c-d-b$. The graph
$B_0\cup H_0$ is planar after every single allowed operation,
as shown above. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms} now lists the $2{,}104$
possible forms of $B$, with $cd$ required in the retained subdivision.
The enumeration~\supp{E7} keeps those for which $B+ac+bd$
is planar, every single allowed operation makes $B+ac+cd+bd$
planar, $B\cup K_4[A]$ is three-connected, and neither $K$
nor the minor $\Psi_1\cup B$ with $P_w$ shortened to $ef$
has a $K_5$ minor. Nine labeled bridges remain. Up to
interchanging $A_1,A_2$, these are the five displayed forms.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}\label{dis:type-b-reduction}
If $G$ has a bridge of type (b) with at least two interior vertices, then $G\cong\mathfrak{T}_{66}$, or the twins and paths can be chosen as at the start of this section so that one of the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item All three paths are edges.
\item There is a bridge of type (c) with at least two interior vertices.
\item Every bridge with nonempty interior has three attachments.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Let $B$ be such a bridge. After interchanging $A_1,A_2$ if
necessary, Lemma~\ref{dis:type-b-forms} gives $P_x=cd$ and
makes $B$ one of $B_1,\ldots,B_5$. In case (i) of that lemma,
the check in~\supp{E7} gives $G\cong\mathfrak T_{66}$. We may therefore
assume case (ii): every other $(J_1\cup J_2)$-bridge attaches
within $\{c,d,e,f\}$, and the simple-face test for
$(P_m;s_x,t_x)$ is nonplanar. In particular, $af,eb$ are
absent. Write $H_{\mathrm{simp}}$ for this test. It consists
of $P_w$, $cd$, the other bridges, and the added edges $ce,df$.
We consider the five possible forms of $B$.

E8.text:
\begin{proof}
Take $E=\varnothing$ in the first case and $E=\{ab,ac,bc\}$
in the second. In either case, $B+E$ is nonplanar by
the hypothesis or Lemma~\ref{r2:32}, and is contained
in every applicable test of Lemma~\ref{r2:four-tests}.
By Lemma~\ref{r2:test-minors}, it is a $K_5$-minor-free minor
of $G$. Every applicable test for an allowed minor $B'$ of $B$
contains $B'+E$. By Lemma~\ref{r2:four-tests}, replacing $B$ by $B'$
therefore gives a nontoroidal graph whenever $B'+E$ is nonplanar.
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments $a,b,c,d$ and
added edges $E$, lists every possible $B$.
Adjoin two vertices with each of the neighborhoods
$\{a,b,c\}$ and $\{a,b,d\}$ in the first case, and three
and two, respectively, in the second. This gives $187{,}075$ graphs. The records in~\supp{E8} leave exactly the stated graphs.
Every other graph is excluded by five branch sets of a
$K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices,
or an edge whose deletion or contraction leaves a
nontoroidal graph. These contradict, respectively,
$K_5$-minor-freeness, three-connectivity or minimality.
\end{proof}

E9.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction},
with attachments $x,c,d$ and added edges $xc,xd$,
lists the reduced bridges before $x$ is separated.
Replace each edge $xv$ by $av$ or $bv$ and add
an edge to the interior at $a$ or $b$ if needed,
considering every possible choice. This includes
every reduction above. Adjoin three vertices
with neighborhood $\{a,b,c\}$ and two with
neighborhood $\{a,b,d\}$. The enumeration~\supp{E9} gives $2{,}953$
candidates up to isomorphisms fixing the attachments.
Of these, $2{,}159$ have a $K_5$ minor, $92$ have
a cut of at most two vertices, and $702$
have a proper nontoroidal minor. These exclude
every candidate, so $H$ cannot be planar.
\end{proof}

E10.text:
If $c,d$ lie apart, take one retained form for $D_c$ and one for $D_d$. If exactly one component avoids $c,d$, include one of the eleven bridges of Lemma~\ref{r2:ab-cut-single} and a permitted subset of $\{aw,bw\}$. If two components avoid $c,d$, include the two single vertices adjacent to all of $X$. In this case $aw,bw$ are absent by Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). If $c,d$ lie together, take one retained form for $D_1$ and include those same two single vertices. Keeping the combinations for which $B$ is planar leaves $1{,}471$ candidates. Of these, the obstruction check in~\supp{E10} leaves only $\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{72},\mathfrak T_{73}$, each with exactly one component of $B-X$ avoiding $c,d$.
\end{proof}

E11.text:
If $m=1$, then $D$ is the star with center $x_1$ and leaves $b,c,d$. The center is adjacent to both $u,v$, or to one of them while one of $b,c,d$ is adjacent to the other. If $m=2$, the degrees of $x_1,x_2$ in $D$ sum to four, so both have degree two. Their neighborhoods in $\{b,c,d\}$ meet in one vertex and together contain all three. Thus $D$ is the path $g_1x_1g_2x_2g_3$ for some ordering $g_1,g_2,g_3$ of $b,c,d$. The vertices $x_1,x_2$ are adjacent to different vertices of $\{u,v\}$, or both are adjacent to one and one of $b,c,d$ is adjacent to the other. These choices give the $31$ forms checked in~\supp{E11}, leaving exactly $\mathfrak T_{40},\mathfrak T_{53},\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{73}$.
\end{proof}

E12.text: Together with $p',q'$ and $\Psi_2$, these choices give every possible $G$ in this case. The DRAT coverage check in~\supp{E12} shows that each combination is a subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains a recorded nontoroidal graph as a subgraph. Since $G$ is nontoroidal, it must contain one of the latter graphs, and by minimality it equals that graph. This leaves $\mathfrak T_{51}$ and $\mathfrak T_{72}$. In neither does any of $D_b-b,D_c-c,D_d-d$ consist of two single vertices.

E13.text:
As in Proposition~\ref{r2:ab-cut-outcome}, discard any form having a proper allowed minor that preserves its neighborhood, the required connectivity and which completions in its row are planar. For each row, combine the retained forms of $B_1,B_2$ with all permitted original edges, and restore $p',q'$ at $X$ and $\Psi_2$ at $a,b,c,d$. The checks in~\supp{E13} exclude all $1{,}229$ resulting candidates. Thus the two-component case gives no obstruction, and the one-component and three-component cases give precisely the six graphs in the statement.
\end{proof}

E14.text: The triangle completion of $B_b$ is three-connected by Lemma~\ref{lem:triangle-completion}, since $D_b-b$ is a component of $G-\{b,c,w\}$. It is a minor of $G$, using the internally disjoint paths $bpc$, $bqap'w$ and $cq'w$ for $bc,bw,cw$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. While $D_b$ keeps its neighbors at $c,w$, the four tests depend on $B_b$ only through $B_b+cw+bw$ and $B_b+cw+bc$. Replacing $B_b$ by a proper allowed minor gives an allowed minor of $B$, since its interior stays adjacent to $w$, the vertices $a,c$ keep $p',q'$, and $d$ keeps $w$. By minimality, no such minor keeps both completions nonplanar. Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical}, with $c,w,b$ as $x,y,z$, therefore makes $B_b$ either $Q(b;c,w)$ or one of the two four-cycle forms. The enumeration~\supp{E14} applies Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} after identifying $c,w$ to a vertex $x$, with attachments $b,x$ and added edge $bx$. It then splits $x$ back into $c,w$, assigning each original edge at $x$ to one of them and adding an edge to an interior vertex at whichever has no interior neighbor. With $\Psi_2$, $p',q'$ and $dw$, the three forms above are among its $24$ candidates. Each has a cut of at most two vertices or a proper nontoroidal minor.

E15.text:
Choose one of these nonplanar completions. Its bridge has connected interior, since Lemma~\ref{r2:one-attachment}(ii) would otherwise give two single vertices whose triangle completion is planar. Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of the chosen completion. Since $B_b+cw$ and $B_d+aw$ are planar, the subdivision uses $bc$ or $ad$, respectively. Reduce the chosen bridge while retaining the subdivision, its connected interior and an interior neighbor at each attachment. In the other bridge, keep one interior component, delete the others and contract the retained component to one vertex. Its neighborhood is the full attachment triple by Lemma~\ref{r2:one-attachment}(ii). Both bridges keep their attachment sets, and their interiors remain connected through $w$, so this gives an allowed minor of $B$. The chosen completion stays nonplanar, and in the other three tests the bridge containing $D_b$ is still adjacent to all of $X$. Thus all four tests remain nonplanar, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists every possible $B_b$ with attachments $b,c,w$, added edges $cw,bc$ and required edge $bc$, or every possible $B_d$ with attachments $d,a,w$, added edges $aw,ad$ and required edge $ad$. An original edge $bw$ or $dw$ may lie on the retained subdivision, so that segment is taken both as an edge and as a path with one interior vertex. The records in~\supp{E15} include both choices of the nonplanar completion. Each of the $156$ candidates has nonplanar $B$, a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

E16.text:
Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $B_1+bd+cw$. It uses $bd$, since deleting this edge leaves the planar graph $B_1+cw$. The vertices of this subdivision outside $\{b,c,d,w\}$ may lie in different components of $B_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$. By \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}, every such component has a neighbor at $w$ and at $b$ or $d$. Retain a $b$--$d$ path in $D_1$ and a neighbor of $c$ outside $\{b,c,d,w\}$. Since $D_1$ avoids $c,w$, the internal vertices of the path lie in one component of $B_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$. The chosen neighbor of $c$ lies in one such component as well. Thus at most two further components are needed. By Lemma~\ref{r2:retained-components}, contract each to one vertex and keep a minimal set of attaching edges satisfying \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}. The retained subdivision keeps $B+ac+bd$ nonplanar. In the other three tests, the bridge containing $D_1$ is still adjacent to all of $X$. The conditions in \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity} keep the interior of $B$ connected and give every attachment an interior neighbor. Thus the reduction is allowed and keeps all four tests nonplanar, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists every possible $B_1$, with attachments $b,c,d,w$, added edges $bd,cw$, the original edges $bw,dw$ permitted on the subdivision, the requirements \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}, and at most two further interior components. Adding $a$ and the three pairs of twins gives the $5{,}819$ candidates in~\supp{E16}. Each has nonplanar $B$, a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor.
\end{proof}

E17.text: Suppose first that every triangle completion is planar. By Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement}, every component outside $\Psi_2$ is a single vertex. Thus $G$ is determined by the numbers of vertices with neighborhoods $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,b,d\}$, $\{a,c,d\}$ and $\{b,c,d\}$, together with the presence or absence of $cd$. At least two vertices have each of the first two neighborhoods, and the four counts sum to at most nine. These give the $252$ choices checked in~\supp{E17}. Every graph except $\mathfrak T_9,\mathfrak T_{10},\mathfrak T_{16}$ has a cut of at most two vertices, is toroidal, or has a proper nontoroidal minor. In all three remaining graphs, $cd$ is absent.

E18.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists these bridge forms with $E=\varnothing$ or $E=\{xy\}$, over all choices of $x,y$. Keep the forms whose three two-edge completions are nonplanar and combine each with $\Psi_2$ and the star at $v$. There are two choices for the attachment triple of $B$ and three remaining choices for $N(v)$. These give the $5{,}934$ graphs checked in~\supp{E18}. Each has a cut of at most two vertices, a $K_5$ minor, or a proper nontoroidal minor. Each possibility contradicts a defining property of $G$.
\end{proof}

E19.text:
By Lemmas~\ref{r2:component-count} and~\ref{r2:eight-bridge-forms}, $G$ consists of $\Psi_2$, one to four bridges of the eight listed forms, and possibly $cd$, with at least one bridge having more than one interior vertex. Assigning each form's attachments to three of $a,b,c,d$ in every possible order gives $76$ labeled bridges up to isomorphisms fixing the attachments. Combining these with disjoint interiors under the preceding conditions, allowing repetitions and including or omitting $cd$, gives $3{,}163{,}020$ combinations. We discard combinations with two disjoint twin triples, three distinct twin triples containing the same two vertices, or a bridge with four attachments for some choice of the four twins. These exclusions remain valid when further bridges or $cd$ are added, since only $a,b,c,d$ gain neighbors and none is a degree-three vertex with a twin. Indeed, $a,b$ have degree at least four, while a twin of $c$ would have to be $a$ or $b$ to be adjacent to both $p,q$, and the same argument applies to $d$. Thus existing degree-three twins keep their neighborhoods. If adding $cd$ puts an edge inside one of these neighborhoods, Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a) excludes the graph, and otherwise the twin triples remain. A component with four attachments also retains those attachments when it becomes part of a larger component. We further discard any combination containing a smaller nontoroidal combination, since it has a proper nontoroidal minor. After these exclusions, the checks in~\supp{E19} give a cut of at most two vertices, a torus embedding, or a proper nontoroidal minor for every combination except four. These four graphs are all isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{15}$.\footnote{The search examines $3{,}163{,}020$ combinations and finds one graph, four times.}
\end{proof}

E20.text:
The nonplanar graph $H$ has no $K_5$ minor. If $bd$ is present, Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion} applied to the toroidal graph $G-bd$ makes $H-bd$ planar, so every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $H$ uses $bd$. Replacing $B$ by an allowed minor $B'$ preserves the connected interior and all five attachments, so by Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion} it gives a nontoroidal graph whenever the corresponding completion of $B'$ is nonplanar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with the five attachments and the fixed planar graph on them consisting of $ab,ac,ad,ae$, together with $bd$ when present, gives $217{,}376$ candidates. All except $\mathfrak T_{20},\mathfrak T_{23}$ have a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, a proper nontoroidal minor, or two twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices~\supp{E20}.
\end{proof}

E21.text:
Put $H_2=B+bc+de$ and suppose it is nonplanar.
By Lemma~\ref{r1:triangle-minor},
$B+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is a minor of $G$.
Thus $H_2$ has no $K_5$ minor. Let $B'$ be an
allowed minor of $B$ with $B'+bc+de$ nonplanar.
The graph $B'+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is still a minor
of $G$, so Lemma~\ref{r1:matching-test} makes
$B'+ab+ac+ad+ae$ nonplanar. Thus $\Psi_3\cup B'$
fails both tests of Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-criterion}.
Taking $B'=B$, minimality gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$b,c,d,e$ and added edges $bc,de$,
includes $B$ among $26{,}633$ forms.
Every resulting graph other than $\mathfrak T_{54}$
is toroidal or has a $K_5$ minor or a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E21}, so
$G\cong\mathfrak T_{54}$.
\end{proof}

E22.text: If $B_1$ is empty, then $E=\{bd,ce\}$. Condition (2) of Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-criterion} makes $H_2+bd$ and $H_2+ce$ nonplanar, so $H_3$ is nonplanar. Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-cut} then makes $bd$ or $ce$ a nonedge of $G$, a contradiction. Suppose next that $B_1$ is one bridge. Interchange $b,c$ and $d,e$ simultaneously if necessary so that its attachments are $\{a,b,d\}$, and put $H_4=B_1+ab+ad$. If $E=\varnothing$, condition (2) makes $H_4$ nonplanar. Contracting the interior of $B$ leaves $H_4$ unchanged, so the graph in condition (1) still contains the nonplanar subgraph $H_4$, while condition (2) requires $H_4$ to be planar. Minimality therefore makes the interior of $B$ a single vertex. If $B_1$ is replaced by an allowed minor $B_1'$ with $B_1'+ab+ad$ nonplanar, neither condition (1) nor condition (2) can hold. Thus Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments $a,b,d$ and added edges $ab,ad$, gives the $349$ forms in~\supp{E22}. Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor.

E23.text:
Suppose $B_1+ab+ad$ is planar.
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} gives twins $p',q'$
whose neighborhood $X$ contains $a$. Since $X$ meets
each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ exactly once, it has
the form $\{a,u,v\}$ with
$u,v\in\operatorname{Int}(B_1)$. The same lemma gives
disjoint $b$--$u$ and $d$--$v$ paths.
Choose $p',q',r,z$ as the four twins.
The set $\operatorname{Int}(B)\cup\{b,c,p,q\}$ is
connected because $c$ has a neighbor in the interior of $B$
and $p,q$ join $b$ to $c$. It lies in a component
outside the new $\Psi_3$, with neighbors at $a,d,e$
through $B$ and at $u$ through the $b$--$u$ path.
Since five attachments are excluded, its bridge
has exactly four attachments and at least
$|\operatorname{Int}(B)|+4$ interior vertices, contrary to
the choice of $B$. Thus $B_1+ab+ad$ is nonplanar, and it has no $K_5$ minor.
Let $B_1'$ be an allowed minor of $B_1$ with $B_1'+ab+ad$
nonplanar. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$
and keep only $\Psi_3$, $B_1'$ and the edges at $w$.
The resulting minor is $\Psi_3\cup B_1'+w$, where
$N(w)=\{a,c,d,e\}$. The graph $\Psi_3+w$ contains $K_{3,3}$ with
parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$. Thus, in every torus
embedding of $\Psi_3+w$, each component of the complement
of its closed regular neighborhood is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.
In every such embedding, a facial walk containing
$a,b,d$ has attachment sequence $abad$, up to
cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R7}.
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore
requires $B_1'+ab+ad$ to be planar, a contradiction.
Hence this minor is nontoroidal. Taking $B_1'=B_1$, minimality
gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B_1+w$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$a,b,d$ and added edges $ab,ad$, gives
$349$ possibilities for $B_1$. These are the $349$ forms of
Proposition~\ref{r1:missing-a-outcome} again. Every resulting graph
has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices,
or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E23}.
Thus every other bridge with nonempty interior
has planar triangle completion, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes its interior
a single vertex.
\end{proof}

E24.text:
Suppose $n_e=3$. The applicable row gives a single
nonplanar completion $B+E'$.
By Lemma~\ref{r1:triangle-minor} with $U=B\cup bd$, contracting $bd$ into $d$
gives the minor
$B+ac+ad+ae+cd+de$ of $G$.
Hence $B+E'$ has no $K_5$ minor.
Replacing $B$ by an allowed minor $B'$ preserves the connected interior and all four attachments, so the resulting minor is nontoroidal whenever $B'+E'$ is nonplanar.
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$a,c,d,e$ and added edges $E'$, gives
$9{,}127$ possibilities without $cd$ and $8{,}967$
with $cd$. Every resulting graph has a proper
nontoroidal minor obtained by deleting or
contracting one edge~\supp{E24}, a contradiction.
Thus $n_e=2$, and the first two rows give the
claimed form of $G$ and its two nonplanar completions.
\end{proof}

E25.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}, using $E'$ and requiring $de$ when $B+ac+E$ is planar, therefore includes every possibility. The two choices of $E$ and the two cases for $B+ac+E$ give $66{,}384$ candidates. Every resulting graph is toroidal, has a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor, or is isomorphic to one of thirteen graphs $\mathfrak T_i$~\supp{E25}. Nine have twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices, leaving $\mathfrak T_{14},\mathfrak T_{37},\mathfrak T_{41},\mathfrak T_{59}$.
\end{proof}

E26.text:
By Lemma~\ref{r1:three-attachment-setup}, $ce$ is an edge or is supplied by a component outside $\Psi_3$. Since $e$ is not an attachment of $B$, we may shorten the resulting $c$--$e$ path to $ce$ and retain $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ as a minor of $G$. The same embedding test applies after replacing $B$ by any allowed minor $B'$, so this minor remains nontoroidal whenever $B'+bc$ is nonplanar. By minimality and Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, $B$ is among the $563$ forms in~\supp{E26} with added edge $bc$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except one copy of $\mathfrak T_{41}$, for which $B+bd+cd$ is planar. This contradicts our assumption.
\end{proof}

E27.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r1:abd-others}
Suppose a bridge $B$ with attachments $\{a,b,d\}$ has no planar completion by two edges. Then every other bridge with nonempty interior has attachments $\{a,b,d\}$ or $\{a,c,e\}$, and every cross edge is $bd$ or $ce$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
First suppose another bridge has attachments $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,d,e\}$,
$\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{c,d,e\}$. Contract its interior to a vertex $v$.
In the first three cases, \eqref{r1:availability} gives the edge $ce$
or a $c$--$e$ path through a component outside $\Psi_3$. Neither $B$
nor the bridge contracted to $v$ has both $c,e$ as attachments, so we
may shorten this path to $ce$ while keeping both bridges intact up to
the contraction to $v$. Retain $\Psi_3$, $B$, the edges at $v$, and
$ce$ in the first three cases. In each case the retained graph outside
$\operatorname{Int}(B)$ is nonplanar, so every face in a torus embedding
of that graph is a disk. The facial walks containing $a,b,d$ have
sequence $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when $N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$
\ \supp{R10}. The test for $abad$ is $B+ab+ad$, and the test for
$abd$ is the triangle completion, which contains $B+ab+ad$.
Since $B+ab+ad$ is nonplanar, Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}
makes the retained minor nontoroidal. By minimality it is $G$.
The same argument applies to any allowed minor $B'$ for which
$B'+ab+ad$ is nonplanar. Thus Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
gives the $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$. Every resulting graph
has a proper nontoroidal minor except two with $N(v)=\{c,d,e\}$.
Both have $B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E27}, contrary to hypothesis.

E28.text:
Suppose $B+ad$ is nonplanar. If an allowed minor $B'$ keeps
$B'+ad$ nonplanar, then both completions in~\eqref{r1:two-cap-test}
remain nonplanar. Replacing $B$ by $B'$ therefore keeps $H_1$
nontoroidal, and Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms} gives the $563$
forms with added edge $ad$. Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor
or a proper nontoroidal minor except four in the $cd$ case,
$\mathfrak T_{52},\mathfrak T_{57},\mathfrak T_{58},\mathfrak T_{59}$.
In the first three, some two twin triples meet in zero or two vertices.
In the last, some choice of the four twins gives a bridge with four
attachments~\supp{E28}. Each contradicts our assumptions, so $B+ad$
is planar.

E29.text:
For $n_c=n_e=2$, the construction gives $31{,}063$ candidates up to
isomorphism fixing $a,b,c,d,e$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a), we exclude any candidate
having a degree-three vertex with two adjacent neighbors. We also
exclude any candidate for which some choice of the four twins gives a
bridge with four or five attachments. Both exclusions still apply when
$n_c$ or $n_e$ increases, since each new vertex is adjacent only to
vertices among $a,b,c,d,e$. In the first exclusion, the recorded
degree-three vertex lies outside these five, so it keeps the same
three neighbors. In the second, the four twins used in the check also
lie outside these five, so they still define the same copy of $\Psi_3$.
The old component lies in a component outside this copy that still
has all four or five original attachments.

This leaves $193$ candidates for $n_c=n_e=2$, giving $965$ cases
over the five choices of $(n_c,n_e)$. Of these, $172$ are toroidal
and $782$ have a proper nontoroidal minor. The remaining $11$ are
copies of the five graphs in the statement~\supp{E29}.
\end{proof}

R1.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{dis:faces}
Every torus embedding of $\Psi_1$ is cellular with five faces.
For some $k\in\{1,2,3\}$, write
$\{i,j\}=\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{k\}$.
Omitting the twins from the boundary walks, these faces are
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item two faces, each following
$s_iP_it_i,t_jP_j^{-1}s_j$ and meeting no other path.
\item one face following
$s_kP_kt_k,t_y,t_kP_k^{-1}s_k,s_x$, where
$x,y\in\{i,j\}$ may be equal.
\item two other faces meeting the paths exactly at
$\{s_k,s_{x'}\}$ and $\{t_k,t_{y'}\}$, respectively,
where $\{x,x'\}=\{y,y'\}=\{i,j\}$.
\end{enumerate}
All twelve choices of $k$, $x$ and $y$ occur.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The graph $\Psi_1$ is connected and nonplanar, as $\Psi_1-z$ is a subdivision of
$K_{3,3}$ with parts $A_1$ and $\{p,q,r\}$, so its torus embeddings are
cellular by Youngs's theorem. Subdividing an edge does not change the faces,
so we may take each $P_i$ to be an edge. Up to automorphisms of $\Psi_1$,
there are exactly two torus embeddings~\supp{R1}, shown in Figure~\ref{fig:F-torus}. Their boundary walks,
after permuting the indices, give (i)--(iii), with $x=y$ in one and
$x\ne y$ in the other. Permuting the indices of both triples
simultaneously is an automorphism of $\Psi_1$, so the first gives the six
choices with $x=y$ and the second the six with $x\ne y$.
\end{proof}

R2.text: Suppose (a) holds, and let $B$ be the unique $\Psi_1$-bridge, whose interior must lie entirely in one facial disk $F$. In~\supp{R2} we record the cyclic sequences of attachment appearances, including repeated appearances, for all possible faces $F$ containing all four attachments in all possible toroidal embeddings of $\Psi_1/s_3t_3$. Up to cyclic shift and reversal, all such sequences also occur around a face in some torus embedding of $\Psi_1$, with the exception of $a,b,c,d$. For those other sequences, the Jordan--Schoenflies theorem allows us to transfer the drawing of $B$ and obtain a toroidal embedding of $H$.

For case (b), we may use the same argument, restricting to the case where attachment $d$ is unused. Read the facial boundary walks in~\supp{R2} for $\Psi_1/s_3t_3$ and $\Psi_1$, recording only appearances of $a,b,c$. Every such sequence containing $a,b,c$ for the contracted graph also occurs for $\Psi_1$. In particular, the order $a,b,c$ occurs in the simple face with order $a,b,d,c$ by leaving $d$ unused. Transferring the drawing of the bridge to the corresponding face therefore gives a torus embedding of $H$. This completes both (a) and (b).

If the region is an annulus, the boundary attachment sequences are $a,c\mid b$, $a,c\mid b,d$, $a\mid b$ or $a\mid b,d$. Each also occurs for $\Psi_1$ by~\supp{R2}, so Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} lets us insert $H_1$ and obtain a torus embedding of $H$.

If it is a disk, the sequences are $a,b$, $a,b,c$, $a,b,d$, $a,b,c,d$ or $a,c,d,b,d,c$. For $\Psi_1$, take the disk drawings of its two simple faces and identify only their boundary copies of $P_1$. The resulting disk has the last sequence. It also gives $a,b,c$ and $a,b,d$ by using the appearances after $b$, so only $a,b,c,d$ with all four attachments remains to be considered.

R3.text:
We establish the final restrictions before enumerating the
possible forms. Suppose neither $h_b$ nor $bc$ occurs. Contract
$cf$ and take a torus embedding of this proper minor. Identify
the two boundary copies of $P_1$ in its incident facial disks,
keeping all other boundary appearances distinct. The path
$P_1$ now lies inside the resulting region apart from its ends.
The rotation calculation~\supp{R3} gives three possible regions:
an annulus with attachment sequence $ac\mid bd$, or a disk with
attachment sequence
\[
a,c,b,d,c\qquad\text{or}\qquad a,c,b,c,d,c.
\]
Every $\Psi_1$-bridge inside $B$ meets the interior of $P_1$,
so lies in this region. No other face contains both $a,d$,
so any present $h_a$ or $ad$ lies there as well. Thus the
region contains $B\cup H_{\mathrm{ext}}$.

R4.text:
Suppose $G$ has a torus embedding and restrict it to $K$.
The connected interior of $B$ lies in one face $F$, whose
boundary contains all four attachments. For each of the
three pairs $(n_c,n_d)$, the rotations of $K$ and their
boundary attachment sequences are given in~\supp{R4}.
Let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular neighborhood of $K$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, if $\mathcal N$ has
genus one, every complementary region is a disk.
If it has genus zero, the complementary regions are disks
together with exactly one annulus or one torus with an
open disk removed. For a disk face, let $H_0$ consist of
the attachments and the edges joining consecutive
attachments on its boundary, as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}.

Suppose the retained graph has a torus embedding. Since $B$ joins $c,d$, a genus-one regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$ would give $B$ a planar two-edge completion by Lemma~\ref{r2:cellular-center}. Its regular neighborhood therefore has genus zero. In this case each boundary walk contains at most two distinct attachment labels~\supp{R4}. Both $B$ and the star at $v$ have three attachments, so each requires a region with at least two boundary components. By Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} they lie in the same annulus. Since together they meet all four attachments, the boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$ or $ad\mid bc$~\supp{R4}.

Suppose a shortening in (i) or (ii) of
Lemma~\ref{r2:cycle-restoration} is
possible. It keeps the interior connected
and preserves all three attachments,
giving a proper minor of $G$.
Take a torus embedding of this minor.
The subgraph $\Psi_2$ and every bridge's attachments are unchanged.
If a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$ has genus zero, no boundary
walk contains three attachments or both $c,d$~\supp{R4}. The shortened
bridge therefore cannot lie in a disk or a torus with one open disk
removed, since each has only one boundary walk. Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}
then forces an annulus, containing every bridge with three attachments
and $cd$ if present. Thus the disk and annulus tests apply.
For a disk containing the shortened bridge, take $H=C_F$, the boundary
cycle in its planar test graph. For an annulus, the additions still meet
all four vertices, so its boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$ or $ad\mid bc$.
Take $H$ to consist of the two added
edges of the annulus test together
with $cd$ or another bridge.
The edge $cd$ joins the two added
edges, and any bridge with three
attachments meets both. Thus $H$
is connected, contains all four
attachment appearances, and avoids
the interior of the shortened bridge. Lemma~\ref{r2:cycle-restoration}
therefore restores $B$ in the planar
test graph, keeping the other edges
and their attachment appearances fixed.
Lemma~\ref{lem:embedding-extension}
or Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}
then gives a torus embedding of $G$,
a contradiction.

R5.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r2:degree-four}
No three-connected obstruction has twin pairs with neighborhoods $\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\}$ and $\deg(b)=4$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Suppose $\deg(b)=4$. Every component outside $\Psi_2$
then has neighborhood $\{a,c,d\}$ by three-connectivity.
Let $B_1$ consist of their bridges and $cd$, if present,
so $G=\Psi_2\cup B_1$. By minimality, $G-z$ has a torus
embedding. All bridges in $B_1$ lie in the same face $F$
of $H=\Psi_2-z$, since each meets $d$ and $\deg_H(d)=1$. Record only $a,c,d$ on the boundary walks of $F$.
If consecutive appearances are equal, move their incident
edges to one appearance along the intervening boundary arc,
preserving their order. Since $B_1$ meets both $c,d$,
the rotation table~\supp{R5} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} leave only the disk sequences
$acd,acad,acacd$ and the annular pairs $ad\mid ac,ad\mid c$. We show that $B_1$ can be drawn in an annulus with $a_1,d$
on one boundary and $a_2,c$ on the other, allowing the edges
at $a$ to use $a_1$ or $a_2$. The annular cases already give
this, with $a_2$ unused for $ad\mid c$. In a disk case,
separate the appearances and use the boundary order
$a_1,c_1,a_2,c_2,d$, leaving positions unused where needed.
Draw $c_1c_2,c_1a_2,a_1d$ outside the disk without crossings,
then contract $c_1c_2$ to recover $c$. The resulting graph
is planar, with $a_1,a_2$ distinct and $a_1d,a_2c$ added.
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} gives the required drawing (Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-annulus-construction}(d)--(f)). A planar embedding of $\Psi_2$ has faces $apcqa$ and $ardza$.
Remove an open disk from each and join the new boundary
circles by a cylinder. This gives a torus embedding with
an annular face $ac\mid ad$. Insert the drawing of $B_1$,
with the edges at $a_2$ reaching $a$ between $ap,aq$ and
those at $a_1$ reaching $a$ between $ar,az$.
This embeds $G$ on the torus (Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-annulus-construction}(a)--(c)), a contradiction.
\end{proof}

R7.text:
Suppose $B_1+ab+ad$ is planar.
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} gives twins $p',q'$
whose neighborhood $X$ contains $a$. Since $X$ meets
each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ exactly once, it has
the form $\{a,u,v\}$ with
$u,v\in\operatorname{Int}(B_1)$. The same lemma gives
disjoint $b$--$u$ and $d$--$v$ paths.
Choose $p',q',r,z$ as the four twins.
The set $\operatorname{Int}(B)\cup\{b,c,p,q\}$ is
connected because $c$ has a neighbor in the interior of $B$
and $p,q$ join $b$ to $c$. It lies in a component
outside the new $\Psi_3$, with neighbors at $a,d,e$
through $B$ and at $u$ through the $b$--$u$ path.
Since five attachments are excluded, its bridge
has exactly four attachments and at least
$|\operatorname{Int}(B)|+4$ interior vertices, contrary to
the choice of $B$. Thus $B_1+ab+ad$ is nonplanar, and it has no $K_5$ minor.
Let $B_1'$ be an allowed minor of $B_1$ with $B_1'+ab+ad$
nonplanar. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$
and keep only $\Psi_3$, $B_1'$ and the edges at $w$.
The resulting minor is $\Psi_3\cup B_1'+w$, where
$N(w)=\{a,c,d,e\}$. The graph $\Psi_3+w$ contains $K_{3,3}$ with
parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$. Thus, in every torus
embedding of $\Psi_3+w$, each component of the complement
of its closed regular neighborhood is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.
In every such embedding, a facial walk containing
$a,b,d$ has attachment sequence $abad$, up to
cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R7}.
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore
requires $B_1'+ab+ad$ to be planar, a contradiction.
Hence this minor is nontoroidal. Taking $B_1'=B_1$, minimality
gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B_1+w$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$a,b,d$ and added edges $ab,ad$, gives
$349$ possibilities for $B_1$. These are the $349$ forms of
Proposition~\ref{r1:missing-a-outcome} again. Every resulting graph
has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices,
or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E23}.
Thus every other bridge with nonempty interior
has planar triangle completion, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes its interior
a single vertex.
\end{proof}

R8.text:
For each of these twelve choices, the attachment sequences from
all rotations of $G-\operatorname{Int}(B)$ are recorded in~\supp{R8}.
In genus one, Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}
gives the disk tests. In genus zero, no boundary
walk contains all four attachments, and the only
possible annulus meeting all four is $ac\mid de$, with test $B+ac+de$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}.
Omitting edge sets that contain another gives the
table. Every listed test comes from a recorded
rotation, so its planarity also gives a torus embedding.

R9.text: Consider a torus embedding of $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$. If a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_3+ce$ has genus one, the facial walks containing $b,c,d$ have attachment sequences $bcd$ or $bcdc$~\supp{R9}. Both disk tests require $B+bc$ to be planar. If the neighborhood has genus zero, no boundary walk contains all three attachments, so $B$ must lie in an annulus. The only possible boundary sequences are $bc\mid ad$ and $bc\mid de$~\supp{R9}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}, the corresponding tests are $B+bc+ad$ and $B+bc+de$. Each is planar exactly when $B+bc$ is planar, since the extra vertex $a$ or $e$ has degree one. Conversely, take the plane embedding of $\Psi_3+ce$ in~\supp{R9} with $b,c$ on one facial walk and $a,d$ on another. Remove an open disk from each face and join the two boundary circles by a cylinder. If $B+bc$ is planar, Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} places $B$ in the resulting annulus $bc\mid ad$. Thus $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ is toroidal exactly when $B+bc$ is planar.

R10.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r1:abd-others}
Suppose a bridge $B$ with attachments $\{a,b,d\}$ has no planar completion by two edges. Then every other bridge with nonempty interior has attachments $\{a,b,d\}$ or $\{a,c,e\}$, and every cross edge is $bd$ or $ce$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
First suppose another bridge has attachments $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,d,e\}$,
$\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{c,d,e\}$. Contract its interior to a vertex $v$.
In the first three cases, \eqref{r1:availability} gives the edge $ce$
or a $c$--$e$ path through a component outside $\Psi_3$. Neither $B$
nor the bridge contracted to $v$ has both $c,e$ as attachments, so we
may shorten this path to $ce$ while keeping both bridges intact up to
the contraction to $v$. Retain $\Psi_3$, $B$, the edges at $v$, and
$ce$ in the first three cases. In each case the retained graph outside
$\operatorname{Int}(B)$ is nonplanar, so every face in a torus embedding
of that graph is a disk. The facial walks containing $a,b,d$ have
sequence $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when $N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$
\ \supp{R10}. The test for $abad$ is $B+ab+ad$, and the test for
$abd$ is the triangle completion, which contains $B+ab+ad$.
Since $B+ab+ad$ is nonplanar, Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}
makes the retained minor nontoroidal. By minimality it is $G$.
The same argument applies to any allowed minor $B'$ for which
$B'+ab+ad$ is nonplanar. Thus Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
gives the $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$. Every resulting graph
has a proper nontoroidal minor except two with $N(v)=\{c,d,e\}$.
Both have $B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E27}, contrary to hypothesis.

R11.text:
It remains to rule out a bridge on $\{b,c,d\}$ and the edge $cd$.
If there is such a bridge, contract its interior to $v$. As above,
we may retain $ce$, since this bridge has no attachment at $e$.
If $cd$ is an edge, retain $cd$ and $ce$. The resulting minor is,
respectively,
\[
H_1=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+v
\qquad\hbox{or}\qquad
H_1=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+cd.
\]
In either graph, $r,z$ are adjacent to each of $a,d,e$, and $c$
joins those same three vertices by $cpa$, by $cvd$ or $cd$, and by
$ce$. These paths give a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in
$H_1-\operatorname{Int}(B)$, so every face in a torus embedding of
this graph is a disk. For each choice of $H_1$, the facial sequences
containing $a,b,d$ are $abad$, $adbd$ and $abd$~\supp{R11}.
The first two test $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$, respectively.
The last tests the triangle completion, which contains both.
Thus Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} gives
\begin{equation}\label{r1:two-cap-test}
H_1\text{ is toroidal}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B+ab+ad\text{ is planar or }B+ad+bd\text{ is planar}.
\end{equation}
Both completions are nonplanar, so $H_1$ is nontoroidal and
minimality gives $G=H_1$.
